business_problem: Medtronic’s teams were spending too much time manually matching invoices, proof-of-delivery documents, and purchase orders, which slowed cash-flow-related processes, introduced errors, and kept staff away from more strategic work.
solution_summary: Medtronic partnered with IBM Consulting and IBM Neudesic to deploy the Document Intelligence Platform Accelerator, an AI-powered automation layer built on Microsoft technology. The platform ingests invoices, proof-of-delivery files, and purchase orders, then uses machine learning and generative AI to extract and match information even when documents contain poor scans, stamps, or inconsistent layouts. IBM Neudesic customized the accelerator so it fit Medtronic’s existing workflows rather than forcing a new manual review process, and the first departmental rollout was completed in only four weeks. Because the system automates the matching step rather than simply flagging issues, teams can process documents at a much higher rate while reserving human effort for exceptions and higher-value analysis. The project therefore improved both operational accuracy and the financial workflow around open receivables, showing how document intelligence can produce immediate business value in a global healthcare operation.

data_flow: Invoices, proof-of-delivery files, and purchase orders are ingested into the DIP Accelerator, AI extracts and matches the relevant fields across the documents, and the resulting match decisions are pushed back into Medtronic’s credit-services and supply-chain workflows for faster resolution.
business_outcome: Medtronic dramatically reduced processing time, improved matching accuracy, and freed staff for strategic work while also helping reduce open accounts receivable and improve cash flow.
